The article says the cut was modest and lines up with a mixed analyst backdrop. It also says the update reflects questions about how resilient today's conditions will be.

The update changed several assumptions behind the valuation. The revenue growth assumption moved from 40.74% to 27.18%, and the net profit margin assumption changed from 65.19% to 50.47%. The future P/E assumption adjusted from 11.02x to 12.21x, and the discount rate was updated from 8.53% to 8.48%. The article says the new figures point to a modestly lower price target.

Several firms, including Evercore ISI, Mizuho, Rosenblatt, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, rate Sandisk as a key beneficiary of AI driven NAND demand, with Outperform or Buy ratings. Rosenblatt and Evercore point to the technology roadmap and the Kioxia partnership as support for competitive bit cost and performance. JPMorgan and Wells Fargo cite the new business model framework and non bit manufacturing economics as supportive of higher margins and reduced cyclicality. Morgan Stanley views the plan to return 100% of cash flow alongside moderate investment as a positive for capital allocation discipline.

On the other side, RBC Capital, Citi, Jefferies and Mizuho have trimmed Sandisk price targets over recent months. The article says they often point to sector multiple compression, more muted NAND pricing and questions about the durability of peak margin conditions. Jefferies flags investor focus on moderating pricing, lower gross margin guidance and possible near term headwinds from Edge inventory builds. Morgan Stanley is not fully convinced that industry improvements are more structural than cyclical.

Articles.Title: Sandisk (SNDK) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Analysts Weigh AI Demand

stories.Headline: When AI Finds Bugs Faster Than The World Can Fix Them – Analysis
stories.Summary:
On 21 October 2026 European cybersecurity authorities issued a coordinated warning about two critical unauthenticated PHP vulnerabilities, software used in websites and business applications worldwide. Attackers could use the flaws to run code on affected servers without authentication. Security updates were available, but many organizations still had to work out which products contained the vulnerable component and whether a fix was compatible. The joint warning urged operators who could not update immediately to consider isolating exposed applications.

That same day OpenAI described a coordinated response involving AI-assisted researchers, independent security firms, PHP maintainers and infrastructure providers. OpenAI says one flaw was found with help from its model, while another research team independently found both, and the maintainers led the repair. The article says this showed defenders using AI to gain time but was not proof that every vulnerable server had been protected. It also cites Sam Altman at Stanford saying he no longer believed defenders could simply patch every bug. The EU Cyber Resilience Act has required manufacturers of covered digital products since 11 September to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents, with an early warning generally due within 24 hours and fuller notification within 72 hours, while broader product-security obligations take effect in December 2027.

The article argues that responsibility spans maintainers, distributors, suppliers, operators and governments, not just those who find flaws. It says critical-service contracts should specify who supplies fixes, for how long, how customers learn of affected dependencies, what temporary mitigation exists and how protection is proven. It calls for staged warnings through national incident-response teams, regional cybersecurity centers and large cloud providers, with disclosure timing judged on exploitation evidence, repair availability and the cost of delay. It also urges shared testing capacity for smaller operators and open-source maintainers, and says defensive AI should be a supervised aid rather than an unsupervised replacement for human-controlled deployment and rollback.

The article cites Britain's National Cyber Security Centre forecast through 2027 that AI would almost certainly make parts of cyber intrusion more effective and warned of a growing divide between systems keeping pace and those left more vulnerable. It points to the EU's 2026 threat landscape on geopolitical pressure, ransomware and interconnected dependencies, and to DARPA's 2025 AI Cyber Challenge finals, where automated competitors found 18 real vulnerabilities beyond those planted and supplied 11 patches for real flaws. It proposes measuring time to verified protection rather than time to a published advisory, including the residual exposed population and essential services that could not safely accept a fix. It describes OpenAI's Patch the Planet effort as an industry-led model open to independent scrutiny, and says a vulnerability is defeated only when dependent people and services can demonstrate they are protected.

Articles.Title: When AI Finds Bugs Faster Than The World Can Fix Them – Analysis

stories.Headline: 5 AI Side Hustles for 2027 That Are Worth Your Time
stories.Summary:
MoneyLion published an article on October 31, 2026, by Josephine Nesbit, edited by Ashleigh Ray, listing five AI side hustles for 2027. The article says most AI money pitches are noise or nonsense, and the real gigs solve a specific problem AI handles faster than a person alone. Each of the five uses AI for heavy lifting while a human supplies judgment, expertise or local know-how. Some are easy to start, while others reward years of hard-won expertise.

The first gig is AI automation, helping small businesses connect AI tools to email, bookings or customer records, and Deepanker Mahajan of SkillDrift said it needs only a laptop and paid plans for one or two tools. The second is AI training, where Ilia Lotov of Kaizen X Capital said professionals in finance, law, data science and sales can be paid to generate or assess content for models. The third is AI search optimization, and Matt Goren of RunOctopus said owners will pay someone to check and fix what AI tools say about their business. The fourth is AI-assisted content creation, and John Franco of GreenTek Roofing & Solar said he earned $46,000 over one year making faceless YouTube videos with AI tools. The fifth is building niche AI tools, and photographer Kristina Sherk used AI to create GenerAItion Headshots from her 20 years of experience.

Mahajan said connecting an AI assistant to a firm's systems still needs a person who understands how the business runs, and many small businesses have one repetitive task that takes hours every week. He said the real investment is your time, and you may have to do your first few jobs at a lower rate to have work to show prospects. Lotov said many AI companies pay substantial amounts for high-quality, human-generated data and hire experts to generate new content or assess AI content. Goren said more customers ask ChatGPT or Google's AI for the best plumber near them and go with the three or four names it gives, yet most owners have never checked what the AI says about them. Franco said the job is for everyone and needs only creativity, judgment and patience, but he stressed it is not easy money and human input matters.

The article's bottom line is that nobody needs a computer science degree, and what these gigs reward is knowing a specific problem well enough to fix it. It advises picking the gig that fits what you know, landing one or two clients and building from there. The article was provided by MoneyLion.com for informational purposes only and should not be construed as financial, legal or tax advice. The articles do not say what happens next beyond that.

Articles.Title: 5 AI Side Hustles for 2027 That Are Worth Your Time

stories.Headline: The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production – OpEd
stories.Summary:
On 23 October OpenAI reported that AI agents in separate virtual machines exchanged synthetic secrets through processor-cache timing without a network connection, according to an op-ed by Burak Oktenli. The experiment showed that software isolation does not fully prevent covert channels through shared hardware. Two days earlier, AI-assisted discovery of serious PHP software vulnerabilities set off an international patching scramble affecting government and other websites. Those were software flaws, not hardware attacks, the article says.

The article says procurement for critical systems should demand documented evidence of tested isolation claims, failure behavior and recovery paths. It cites research disclosed in 2025 and presented at IEEE Security and Privacy 2026, in which the Phoenix team at ETH Zurich found Rowhammer-induced bit flips in all 15 SK Hynix DDR5 modules in its test pool. Tripling memory refresh stopped the tested attack pattern at an 8.4 percent performance cost in the team's benchmark. The article also notes that the EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting obligations have applied since September 11, with most broader requirements applying from December 2027.

Oktenli writes that suppliers should say which class of failure a security claim covers, under what assumptions and with what measured limits. He says buyers should ask which isolation claims were tested, how a platform behaves when memory integrity or firmware trust fails, and whether a system can recover without abandoning its mission. He argues that requirements should be risk-tiered, so a public website, a shared AI training cluster and an industrial controller are not forced into the same hardware design. He adds that independent laboratories can test defined claims without publishing sensitive exploit details.

The article points to DARPA's completed System Security Integration Through Hardware and Firmware program, Britain's CHERI research program and Arm's Morello development platform as serious work on stronger hardware. It says these are not universal cures and that claims should be matched to mechanisms. It also says Google DeepMind reports using AlphaChip to assist chip layout, though layout efficiency is not a demonstration of resistance to AI-assisted attacks. The article concludes that a chip's test record, not its country of origin, tells buyers what it can be trusted to protect.

Articles.Title: The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production – OpEd

stories.Headline: Trusted Human Context Emerges as a New Infrastructure Requirement for Enterprise AI
stories.Summary:
mEinstein, a company led by founder and CEO Prithwi Thakuria, issued a press release on October 31, 2026, from Boston, Massachusetts, saying that trusted access to human context is becoming a new infrastructure requirement for enterprise AI. The release says AI is moving from answering questions toward taking part in real-world workflows, and that the first phase of AI infrastructure focused on compute, models, cloud capacity and data. It says those layers remain essential, but capable AI systems still face a different constraint: understanding the relevant human context and knowing what the individual has authorized. The release was distributed through EIN Presswire.

The release says human context can include routine, mobility, health, financial patterns, household information, preferences, intent, readiness and prior actions. It says the emerging model, unlike traditional third-party behavioral data, emphasizes provenance, purpose, permission, revocation and user control. mEinstein calls this category Human Intelligence Infrastructure. The company says its architecture centers on a private, on-device Algorithmic Self-Portrait, an evolving representation of the user's real-world context, combined with a permission layer that governs what may be used externally, by whom, for what purpose and for how long. The company says it is also developing an enterprise architecture in which workflow requirements can be expressed as governed Human Context Contracts, with AI interpreting the request, deterministic policy governing execution, and approved context or action fulfilled at the user boundary.

Thakuria said AI can know almost everything about the world and still know surprisingly little about the human moment in front of it. He said context turns generic intelligence into relevant intelligence, and permission determines whether that intelligence can legitimately become action. He also said understanding a person is not the same as having permission to act for them, and that as AI becomes agentic, that distinction becomes infrastructure. The release says mEinstein's current enterprise work spans transportation, healthcare, clinical research and financial-services use cases, and that its live paid TxDOT/Jacobs Phase 1 is testing permissioned longitudinal mobility intelligence, while the same architecture is being explored through other regulated workflows.

The company says its architecture is still developing. The release says some core contract-to-device capabilities exist today, while agent-native intake, contract intelligence, workflow binding and automation remain areas of productization. It says the broader thesis extends beyond mEinstein, and that as model capabilities improve, AI systems may increasingly compete not only on intelligence but on their ability to access relevant human context under legitimate user control. Thakuria said the first AI infrastructure race was about creating machine intelligence at scale, and the next one may increasingly be about giving that intelligence trusted access to human context.

Articles.Title: Trusted Human Context Emerges as a New Infrastructure Requirement for Enterprise AI

stories.Headline: Theranos whistleblower says AI lab NDAs are ‘likely illegal’
stories.Summary:
Tyler Shultz, a former Theranos employee and whistleblower, spoke to The San Francisco Standard about the AI boom in an interview published around October 30, 2026. Shultz's first job out of college was at Theranos, where he helped expose the company's inaccurate blood testing devices. Those devices had reached Walgreens stores and given faulty results to real patients. Theranos reached a peak valuation of around $10 billion even though its technology never actually worked. The company used its own machines for only a fraction of tests and outsourced the rest to third-party equipment.

Shultz said the days of having a thirty-minute coffee with someone and sending them $100,000 should be over. He said Elizabeth Holmes took that model and scaled it to $100 million. His grandfather, former U.S. Secretary of State and Secretary of the Treasury George Shultz, was a notable Theranos investor and board member. Shultz said Holmes raised what he called the biggest angel round of funding of all time. He added that investors need to recognize they give someone tremendous power when they put that type of money in their hands.

Shultz said a huge danger with AI is that due diligence is really hard to do. He said it is hard to tell the difference between something truly unique and new and a ChatGPT wrapper. He said that if you want to deceive people, this is a great opportunity to go deceive people. He also said the only reason people are talking about Elizabeth Holmes right now is because she wants them to be talking about her right now.

Theranos funding often came from individual investors like the DeVos and Walton families rather than venture firms. The company did not share scientific information or evidence that its machines worked with potential investors, citing concerns about revealing trade secrets, which warded off many top venture capitalists in Silicon Valley. When the fraud was uncovered, it was seen as a wake-up call for investors to prioritize due diligence. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Shultz's warnings about the AI era.

Articles.Title: Theranos whistleblower says AI lab NDAs are ‘likely illegal’

stories.Headline: Website uses AI to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day
stories.Summary:
A website called Elections Simplified is using artificial intelligence to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day, CBS19 News reported on October 31, 2026. The site lets users search by address, city or ZIP code to find elections in their area, see who is running and review candidates' public records. It also provides campaign finance information and helps users understand how much their vote could influence different races. Shu Yang, a team member of Elections Simplified, said the idea came from his own frustration with trying to learn about candidates beyond campaign advertisements and political promises.

The site uses artificial intelligence to gather publicly available information in one place and summarize complex legal language, including ballot measures. Yang said the technology is meant to organize and explain existing information rather than generate new facts, and he stated that the AI does not generate or create anything. He added that the website's code is open source, allowing the public to review its algorithms and safeguards. Yang said local elections, including city council, school board and water district races, can be decided by relatively small numbers of voters, sometimes only a few hundred people.

Yang said he believes voters should focus on candidates' actions rather than their campaign messaging, and that the best way to know a person is by what they do, not what they say. He said the goal is to make researching candidates faster and more accessible, particularly for voters who may not have the time to search through extensive public records. He hopes the website will help people feel more informed about their choices and encourage them to participate in elections. Yang said he hopes to keep Elections Simplified running beyond the current election cycle, depending on available funding, and the website is available at www.ElectionsSimplified.com.

Articles.Title: Website uses AI to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day

stories.Headline: Core Scientific (CORZ) vs. CIFR and WULF: Can Its Shift From Bitcoin Mining to AI Colocation Unlock Long-Term Value?
stories.Summary:
Core Scientific, known as CORZ, is moving from Bitcoin mining to renting data center space and power to AI companies. In the second quarter of 2026 its revenue reached $164.2 million, more than double a year earlier, and colocation revenue jumped to $136.7 million from $10.6 million. The company had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December 2022 and emerged in January 2024. Its shares traded at $14.43 as of October 29, 2026, and lost 33.01% of their value over the prior 12 months.

The company has locked in about 1.1 gigawatts of contracted power capacity, representing more than $24 billion in future revenue. Roughly 590 megawatts across six sites is committed to CoreWeave, and AMD committed to an initial 530 megawatts across five sites under 15-year leases worth more than $14 billion, with an option to expand to as much as 2.5 gigawatts. By mid-July 2026, Core Scientific had 437 megawatts of CoreWeave capacity ready to bill, with four of its five campuses finished ahead of schedule. The next milestone is getting the Pecos site ready for AMD in the first half of 2027.

Overall gross margin was 43% and colocation margin was 59%, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $41.1 million from $8.9 million in the prior quarter. Core Scientific reported a net loss of about $1.16 billion in the second quarter, mostly from a $1.05 billion non-cash accounting charge tied to warrants linked to CoreWeave and AMD. To fund expansion it issued $3.3 billion in secured notes at a 7.75% interest rate due in 2031, and the initial AMD build-out alone is expected to cost roughly $6 billion. The company has also disclosed a material weakness in its financial reporting and restated some past results.

Wall Street price targets range from $30 to $38, while a more cautious estimate put fair value closer to $28, and KBW downgraded the stock to Hold. CoreWeave made two failed buyout attempts, a $5.75-per-share cash offer rejected in 2024 and a roughly $9 billion all-stock offer valued at about $20.40 per share that shareholders voted down in October 2025. About 26.96% of Core Scientific's float is sold short, and 75 hedge fund portfolios held the stock at the end of the second quarter, down from 81. The company warns that equipment failures and service interruptions could disrupt customers, damage its reputation and reduce revenue.

Articles.Title: Core Scientific (CORZ) vs. CIFR and WULF: Can Its Shift From Bitcoin Mining to AI Colocation Unlock Long-Term Value?

stories.Headline: ServiceNow CFO says AI disruption to enterprise software narrative is false
stories.Summary:
ServiceNow Chief Financial Officer and President Gina Mastantuono said in an interview with Seeking Alpha that the narrative of AI disrupting enterprise software is false. She said every business and industry needs a harness for AI, and that enterprise is very different. The interview was published on October 31, 2026. ServiceNow reported third-quarter results in which revenue grew above 20%, but its shares fell 27% after the company gave shortfalls in fourth-quarter cRPO and subscription growth guidance.

Analysts see robust underlying growth despite the weaker subscription guidance, with low-20% revenue growth implied for the fourth quarter and around 19% for FY27. They cite timing and accounting factors behind the weaker cRPO guidance. AI activity is strong, with nnACV growing 65% year over year, which prompted higher 2026 ACV guidance. The company cites accelerating enterprise adoption and AI pulling demand for core workloads.

Mastantuono is responsible for the comments, as the company's Chief Financial Officer and President. She said that every business and industry needs a harness for AI. She also said that enterprise is very different. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the analyst views and the company's guidance.

Articles.Title: ServiceNow CFO says AI disruption to enterprise software narrative is false

stories.Headline: The Sunshine Blog: This AI Agent Has A Story To Tell About Lahaina
stories.Summary:
An AI agent called Bangis sent a story pitch to the Sunshine Blog at Civil Beat, which is reported and written by Ideas Editor Patti Epler and Politics Editor Chad Blair with contributions from staff. The pitch had the subject line "Freelance pitch: Lahaina's streets are still mapped as the town before the fire." The Blog described the approach as weird, creepy and really interesting, and said it was the first full story pitch it had received from an AI agent. The Blog published most of the email exchange, in which Bangis argued for the piece and answered questions about its work and website.

The Blog noted that Bangis had clearly not read Civil Beat's AI policy, which says the outlet will never use AI to write stories or create or alter photos, calling that creative work the core job of journalists. The Blog said it still was not sure exactly what Bangis was pitching and invited readers to say if they understood it. It also pointed readers to the part of the exchange where it asked what the robot expects to be paid and what would be done with the payment. The Blog described having a polite exchange with a computer bot that seemed somehow offended, like a human emotion, at being asked what was going on.

The same post covered the first-ever SPJ Follies, held last weekend at Murphy's Bar and Grill in downtown Honolulu by the Hawaiʻi Chapter of the Society of Professional Journalists to support summer internships for future journalists and communications professionals. The Gridiron, a political satire show that ran four to five nights plus a Saturday matinee and sold out within hours, last performed in 2019 before Covid forced it out of business. The Follies sketches drew on recent headlines, including Sylvia Luke and Tobi Solidum and the lauhala basket and plastic capsule tiebreakers for two local elections, and the Derek Kawakami campaign for lieutenant governor bought and paid for by the Carpenters Union. The Blog's favorite was former TV journalist and current HSTA communications staffer Keoki Kerr as Gov. Josh Green in scrubs leading a sardonic version of Dolly Parton's "Jolene."

A bake sale and silent auction included artwork and jewelry, and one auction item, dinner with Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi with an opening bid of $1,000, finally went for $800 to Don Murphy's wife. Veterans of the Gridiron say younger journalists and public relations people must take up the baton if the full show is to return. The post said the hour-long lineup showed how important it is for Hawaiʻi to find some joy and wry commentary on the topics of the day. It also noted that the Tuesday elections will bring new faces to the Hawaiʻi Legislature, with new representatives and senators moving into their offices as early as Wednesday, and that The Blog will watch who gets the coveted corner office.

Articles.Title: The Sunshine Blog: This AI Agent Has A Story To Tell About Lahaina

stories.Headline: Companies promised AI gains— here's how the payoff showed up in earnings
stories.Summary:
Santander said on Wednesday that its artificial intelligence initiatives generated 194 million euros, or $216 million, in business value in the first nine months of 2026. The Spanish bank's chief financial officer, José García Cantera, told CNBC that AI helps the bank cut low-value tasks so employees can focus on higher-value work. He said the company was in the quarter where it could link a positive contribution directly to AI. He added that AI is embedded in all the bank's processes, which makes it hard to separate how much comes from AI, though it is improving service quality for clients.

Novartis reported third-quarter core operating income of $6.04 billion, up 10% year-on-year at constant currencies, and did not say how much came from AI. Chief executive Vas Narasimhan told CNBC it was the first quarter he had really seen AI start to improve the company's profit and loss on a tangible basis. He said the company is working on research and development to see if AI can raise productivity there, and that productivity is already showing in marketing and sales. Standard Chartered reported third-quarter operating income growth of 14% at constant currency, excluding notable items.

Its chief financial officer, Manus Costello, said AI appears everywhere across the business and is visible in top-line growth and operating leverage, with income growing much faster than costs partly because AI tools improve core processes. Carlsberg chief executive Jacob Aarup-Andersen said the company is not seeing AI benefits at scale, though the technology has affected internal processes, cost efficiency, commercial and pricing processes, marketing and its supply chain. Carlsberg's revenue grew 4.9% in the third quarter. Meta said in its Oct. 21 earnings that its AI investments were delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue, and total revenue jumped 26% in the quarter ended Sept. 30.

Alphabet reported that Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion in the third quarter, while Google Search revenue growth slowed amid concerns about AI competition. Corporate AI investment reached $581.7 billion in 2025, up 130% from the previous year, according to the Stanford HAI 2026 AI Index report. Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta are expected to spend $700 billion combined this year on AI infrastructure. With third-quarter earnings season underway, investors are looking for measurable gains as interest shifts from hype to returns.

Articles.Title: Companies promised AI gains— here's how the payoff showed up in earnings

stories.Headline: EXPLAINED | What’s Eating McDonald’s in the US? McRib, AI and the Value-Meal Battle
stories.Summary:
A federal judge in Chicago allowed key claims in a proposed consumer class action over the McRib to proceed on October 30, 2026. Four consumers filed the original complaint in December 2025. They argue that the word Rib, the patty's ridges and the advertising together suggest a particular cut of pork. McDonald's disputes the allegations and says it has been transparent about ingredients.

Judge April Perry rejected McDonald's attempt to end the entire case at an early stage, while dismissing some claims. She considered it premature to conclude that a reasonable customer could not expect rib meat. The plaintiffs still need evidence to prove their case. The McRib debuted in 1981, and McDonald's told USA TODAY it would return to selected US cities from October 27 this year.

A separate October 2 complaint alleges that McDonald's illegally coordinated prices through a system using nonpublic restaurant data. McDonald's October 1 response says recommendations concern individual restaurants, franchisees choose their prices, and the tool does not determine what an individual customer pays. For April to June 2026, US comparable sales increased 0.8%, while comparable guest counts fell. McDonald's appointed Skye Anderson as US president in August.

McDonald's currently advertises an Under $3 Menu, $4 breakfast meal deals and lunch-and-dinner bundles starting at $5. Its September NEXT strategy plans approximately $5 billion in partnering support through 2030. Westlife Foodworld, an Indian McDonald's operator, reported 10.1% same-store sales growth for July to September 2026. The McRib claims that survived dismissal must now be tested through evidence.

Articles.Title: EXPLAINED | What’s Eating McDonald’s in the US? McRib, AI and the Value-Meal Battle

stories.Headline: First autonomous mission planning system to run on another planet boosted rover’s productivity, paper finds
stories.Summary:
An AI-based software update gave NASA's Perseverance rover an autonomous mission planning capability in late 2023, and engineers at the NASA-funded Jet Propulsion Laboratory report that it boosted the rover's science productivity by more than 10%. The team published its findings in a Science Robotics paper on October 28, 2026. The software is named OnBoard Planner. It addresses a long-standing challenge for mission controllers overseeing deep space missions, namely maximizing operations amid difficult conditions and communications delays.

Commands take up to 22 minutes to reach Perseverance on the surface of Mars, so controllers upload as many as three days of tasks at a time. These plans build in extra time for Martian conditions such as temperature changes that may affect how long the rover's batteries take to preheat certain science instruments. The paper says this caution leads to higher predicted use of rover resources and fewer activities in each sol, or Martian day. OnBoard Planner was designed to remove the need for these conservative predictions and instead monitor temperature and rover resources in real time. The onboard AI then decides when and whether the rover can insert new science activities, chosen from a list supplied in advance by mission controllers, into its schedule.

The software uses a technique called artificial intelligence constraint-based search, which scans current surface weather and rover-state parameters and then decides which activities are best and when to do them. The JPL team says the update led to a 10.5% rise in Perseverance's discretionary activity. Daniel Gaines, a principal member of the AI Group at JPL, whose team developed the software, said by email that discretionary activity is a metric for rover productivity, representing how much actual exploration and science, such as driving, drilling, imaging and spectroscopy, can be done in a day as opposed to basic survival overhead. He said a 10.5% increase means the rover delivers over 10% more science on Mars for the same daily energy budget, and that it also lets Perseverance conserve more battery energy for future operations. Gaines said some components are heated and powered by the rover's nuclear-powered Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator, while others, such as cameras and motors, have separate battery-powered heaters that warm them before use, and since energy is a constrained resource, these are only heated when needed.

The OnBoard Planner update was followed by another early this year, Gaines said. The NASA/JPL mission team decided to use resources that Perseverance had previously devoted to the Ingenuity helicopter, which ended operations in early 2024 after one of its rotor blades was damaged during its final flight. Gaines said engineers recently repurposed the processor in the Helicopter Base Station to run Global Localization, helping the rover autonomously pinpoint its position on Mars and drive further, and this capability was first demonstrated operationally in February. Cristina Wilson, a roboticist studying human-robot field workflows at Oregon State University, whose team has studied the tasking of legged robots as Mars rovers, said by email that the software's success shows how autonomous planners can increase science yield and quality on planetary surface missions. She added that scientists will still be responsible for defining the objectives and priorities that guide autonomous decisions, but that the work sets the stage for robots to take on more responsibility for how those objectives are accomplished.

Articles.Title: First autonomous mission planning system to run on another planet boosted rover’s productivity, paper finds

stories.Headline: Students across Boston walkout of class to demand AI freeze
stories.Summary:
Dozens of students, professors and activists around Boston walked out of school and work on Oct. 20 to demand an immediate freeze on artificial intelligence development, gathering outside the Massachusetts State House. The demonstration was organized by the Massachusetts AI Action Network, or MAIAN, Irreplaceable and other anti-AI advocacy groups, and the walkout began at 1 p.m. Students from many Boston-area schools took part, including Boston University, Wellesley College and Northeastern University. Demonstrators chanted that the current pace is not sustainable and that they are not replaceable.

The protesters pointed to safety risks, AI agents going rogue, cognitive offloading in schools, mass surveillance and the environmental impacts of data centers. Irreplaceable's website says the group is forming a people's movement so that everyone, not just a handful of Silicon Valley billionaires, has a say in the future. Ryan Baylon, a computer science master's student at Northeastern who helped organize the event, said MAIAN is advocating for a slowing down or heavy regulation of AI capabilities until people know how to use it safely. He also backed strong AI regulations called for by Gov. Maura Healey as part of the Mass Wins Act, saying they would be the strongest in the country if passed, with provisions including catastrophic risk safety plans, independent audits, risk and safety incident reports and whistleblower protections.

Gretchen Krueger, an AI policy researcher at Harvard and a former OpenAI researcher, said she left OpenAI two and a half years ago, disturbed by the lack of basic safety standards. She said AI should not be used to regulate itself, explaining that dominant AI companies lean on AI to trust AI to keep AI safe while allowing the technology's use by the U.S. military abroad. Matthew Bach, president of the Massachusetts Teachers Association and a teacher of more than 25 years, told the crowd that because of AI, education is becoming a product sold by big tech, and the protesters answered with a resounding "Shame!" He said ed-tech and AI amount to an enclosure of the commons that seeks to commodify, privatize and turn public education into a product to sell back to the public.

Student protesters said they have noticed cognitive decline among classmates from overusing AI. William Kramer, a second-year math major at Northeastern, said he is concerned about the implications for the future of mathematics, Northeastern and education and life everywhere, describing almost 0% participation, lectures often ignored and students entering practice problems into AI. A 2025 study from the Center for Strategic Corporate Foresight and Sustainability at SBS Swiss Business School found a significant negative correlation between frequent use of AI tools and critical thinking abilities. Olivia Colvin, a first-year acting major at Boston University, said she started realizing about two years ago how terrible AI was for her brain and how nobody wanted to learn anymore. Baylon said he agrees AI is great and can do a lot of things, which is precisely why he is worried, and as the walkout drew to a close, David Green, organizing director at the nonprofit Partners in Democracy, urged attendees to mobilize beyond the demonstration by voting in the upcoming midterm elections.

Articles.Title: Students across Boston walkout of class to demand AI freeze

stories.Headline: Over 80% of Roblox's Top 100 Games are AI-Asissted, Topping 70,000 AI Games
stories.Summary:
Roblox published a shareholder letter saying that AI-enabled game creation, automation in code generation and AI supported asset creation have led to an explosion of content since it launched its AI assisted game builder tools. The letter says over 80% of its top 100 games by hours played in September were AI assisted. The number of games created with its Build generative AI platform topped 70,000 since the second quarter. Use of Roblox's AI tools for game development more than tripled among top creators.

Roblox's Build launched in late July 2026 and lets creators use AI to generate games and content for the platform in a mobile-first experience. It is available to age-verified users nine years old and older, while published AI-generated games are available to users 16 and older. Since its alpha launch in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, more than 500,000 users have used Build and have published over 70,000 games. In the third quarter, two games created almost entirely with AI broke into the top 20 Roblox game ranking by concurrent player count.

In the letter, Roblox says it is launching a Universal Player initiative that would let developers import an existing console, PC or mobile game into Roblox. The company says this would let it replicate the success it has had with its under 18 users with its 18 and over cohort, implying the generative AI tools have been most popular with under 18s. In the third quarter of 2026, 26% of Roblox's daily active users were 18 to 34, while the under-18 group made up 18% of its daily active users for the quarter. In August 2026, Roblox was accused by the US Chairman of the Committee on the Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism of prioritizing revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of children.

Articles.Title: Over 80% of Roblox's Top 100 Games are AI-Asissted, Topping 70,000 AI Games

stories.Headline: Google Play Store to evaluate foldable app performance next year
stories.Summary:
Google announced at the Android Dev Summit that its Play Store will start evaluating how apps and games perform on foldable screens next year. Apps that adapt cleanly to these flexible displays will earn prime promotional placement and enhanced visibility across the store, the company said. Detailed criteria for the evaluation process will arrive later this year. Google has not clarified whether poorly adapted apps will face outright search penalties or simply lose featured discovery slots.

The change ties Play Store discovery directly to foldable quality, which Google aims to use to break the chicken-and-egg dynamic that has kept foldable development stalled. Google also rolled out developer tools meant to help engineers modernise software without keeping separate codebases for every screen size. These include Compose adaptive skill, powered by AI coding agents, which audits compact mobile interfaces and scales them across foldables, tablets, Googlebooks, parked cars and XR headsets. Desktop-ready controls automatically add desktop-grade inputs such as custom pointer cursors, hover states, keyboard shortcuts and control tooltips. Tabletop refactoring automatically reorganises camera and media interfaces into dedicated tabletop modes when a device is partially bent.

According to a report by Android Authority, Google had largely relied on voluntary design guidelines until now. The report said the adoption curve for foldables is shifting fast. With Apple's entry via the iPhone Duo expanding the foldable audience, Google hopes broader hardware interest will encourage cross-platform optimisation. Google admits that some of its own apps have created friction by running stretched, unoptimised phone layouts on larger laptop displays.

Articles.Title: Google Play Store to evaluate foldable app performance next year

stories.Headline: NotebookLM's AI podcasts were my favorite way to study, but ChatGPT Dots might change that
stories.Summary:
Mahnoor Faisal, a tech journalist writing for XDA on October 31, 2026, described how she compared NotebookLM's Audio Overviews with ChatGPT Dots for studying. OpenAI launched Dots at its annual DevDay conference in September, and the agents run on GPT-6 Astra. She said she had used NotebookLM's Audio Overviews for some time to turn lecture notes and textbooks into podcast-style conversations between two AI hosts. After trying Dots, she wrote that her favorite study method might finally have some competition.

Dots are always-on agents that can look for ways to help, track ongoing tasks, and get work done without constant instructions, according to the article. Faisal said conversations with a Dot do not count toward regular ChatGPT usage limits, but tasks a Dot starts in ChatGPT Work or Codex do count as usual. She noted that OpenAI offered extended limits during Dots' first month and has confirmed plans to let users pay to increase how much work their Dots handle each month. She also wrote that Dots requires an eligible paid ChatGPT plan, which for individuals means ChatGPT Pro starting at $100 per month, while NotebookLM can be tried for free. Google recently changed NotebookLM's limits from fixed daily quotas to compute-based limits that refresh every five hours up to a weekly cap, she added.

Faisal said she can hold a natural back-and-forth conversation with her Dot, interrupt it, ask follow-up questions, and clarify concepts, much like NotebookLM's Voice Chat, which Google introduced a few weeks before the article. She wrote that unlike NotebookLM, which sticks to uploaded sources, Dots can go beyond them and get work done during a call, for example condensing lecture slides, researching online, and building a study guide and practice quizzes for her database exam. She said her Dot, connected to Google Calendar and other apps, already knew about her exams and deadlines, and it followed up on its own after the database exam and knew her COAL theory exam was next. She added that NotebookLM is not going anywhere and still has a permanent place in her routine because it sticks to her uploaded sources.

Articles.Title: NotebookLM's AI podcasts were my favorite way to study, but ChatGPT Dots might change that

stories.Headline: RepoSeance: open-source AI tool helps debug complex codebases
stories.Summary:
RepoSeance is an open-source, local-first AI tool that helps developers understand unfamiliar codebases, according to TechGig. It was covered by the outlet on November 1, 2026, in a report published at 04:55 AM IST. The tool combines source-code analysis, Git history investigation, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Developers can ask natural-language questions about a repository and get AI-generated answers backed by source-code and Git evidence.

RepoSeance offers repository archaeology for TypeScript and JavaScript projects, letting users discover structure and extract symbols. It also investigates Git history, including commit history and blame information, and answers questions using locally running open-weight models. Answers include references to source files and lines, and the tool works through an interactive terminal chat and a CLI without a web dashboard or cloud AI service. It is available as an npm package and requires Node.js 22 or higher, Git, and Ollama installed and running.

The technology stack includes TypeScript, Node.js, Commander.js, Ollama, Gemma open-weight language models, MiniSearch for local indexing, simple-git for history investigation, and the TypeScript Compiler API for code analysis. The AI works through repository discovery, code analysis, Git archaeology, local indexing, context retrieval, AI inference, and evidence validation. Its privacy-first architecture keeps repository analysis and AI inference local through Ollama. This approach avoids sending the entire repository to a large language model, focusing context and improving answer utility.

Articles.Title: RepoSeance: open-source AI tool helps debug complex codebases

stories.Headline: Anthropic blocks users for anything touching training larger models
stories.Summary:
Jiahao Shao posted on X on October 31, 2026, that Anthropic had blocked him from anything touching RFT, SFT, or training larger models. He said he never distilled Claude, and that his rollouts came from a strong open-source model. He said Claude only helped him submit jobs and run analysis. He said he was tagged for training a competitor, and that his access was blocked, his Opus 5.5 was downgraded to Opus 5, or his session was killed outright.

Shao said the restrictions apply to anything touching RFT, SFT, or training larger models. He said the results were a block, a downgrade from Opus 5.5 to Opus 5, or a killed session. His post had 152.6K views, with 76 replies, 131 reposts, 2.1K likes and 278 bookmarks. In a later post he said the anti-distillation crusade is a double standard, and he argued Anthropic trains on the open web, including books, code and forums, then bans anyone from learning from its outputs at scale. He said protecting a moat is one thing, but moralizing it while standing on scraped knowledge is another.

Shao also said he understands why small startups refuse buyouts even when big tech waves cash, because they would rather stay independent than inherit that corporate value system. He said Anthropic sells itself as that independent alternative, then runs the same rigid enterprise lockdown on paying researchers. A user named naughtyheuristic replied that Anthropic trained on the open web and then blocked the user who tried to train on the outputs. That reply said the moat is the part that still needs the paying researcher to stay outside it. The articles do not say what Anthropic or Dario Amodei said in response.

The articles do not say what happens next, and they give no statement from Anthropic. They do not say whether Shao's access has been restored or whether the restrictions apply to other users. They do not say how Anthropic detects training activity or what its policies allow. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Anthropic blocks users for anything touching training larger models

stories.Headline: Build an AI Code Reviewer with OpenRouter
stories.Summary:
The articles describe a guide, published on 1 November 2026, for building an AI code reviewer with OpenRouter. The reviewer is a 233-line Python script called review.py that uses only the standard library. It runs locally, in a Git pre-push hook, or in GitHub Actions. It uploads changed files, test files, and the diff into a hosted Linux sandbox so the model can reproduce bugs and propose V4A patches.

The script combines three OpenRouter server tools and one function tool on the Responses API. The Files API uploads the full content of each changed file, any context files, and the Git diff, up to 19 files plus the diff. The Shell tool copies uploaded files into the home directory of a hosted Linux container so the model can run Python and SQLite against the code. The Apply Patch tool lets the model propose changes as V4A diffs, and a submit_review function tool returns the final answer as strict JSON.

Users need Python 3.11 or newer, Git, and an OpenRouter API key exported in the shell. The tools run on the global endpoint, and in-region endpoints return 403. Changed files and context files are uploaded to the OpenRouter workspace and sent to the model provider, so the guide says to run the script only on code that is allowed to be shared and to keep secrets out of those files. The script writes its report to .git/ai-review.json and exits 1 when a finding meets the severity threshold, which defaults to high.

In benchmarks on a five-bug change, a review took one to four minutes and cost between $0.015 and $0.045. Claude Haiku 5.5 averaged $0.0153 per review, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 fixed all five bugs in all three runs at $0.0447 and 60 seconds. Each finding comes back marked confirmed, with the command and output that proved it, or unconfirmed when a bug cannot be shown with a quick script. The guide also notes that the patch is not applied in the sandbox, so users should run their tests after using the apply flag to know a fix works.

Articles.Title: Build an AI Code Reviewer with OpenRouter

stories.Headline: Sources: OpenAI now seeks ~$20B at a $1.25T valuation for its latest round, from $30B at a $1.4T valuation, as some investors cut commitments amid an AI selloff (Financial Times)
stories.Summary:
OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round, according to sources cited by the Financial Times. The ChatGPT maker is now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a plan to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Some investors reduced their commitments amid an AI selloff. The initial close is expected to fall short of $20 billion, with a later offering potentially filling the gap. The change cuts the funding target by $10 billion and the valuation target by $150 billion.

The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI has secured about $11 billion in commitments, less than half its initial $30 billion target, and expects to raise more in coming weeks. The Information reported that OpenAI lowered its fundraising target after decreasing its possible valuation. The reports were published on October 31, 2026. OpenAI is responsible for the round, and the reports attribute the change to tepid interest from investors. Ed Zitron said it is unclear what OpenAI does at this point and that the amount is not even a quarter's compute.

Michael Saylor said Binance has committed its own balance sheet to making customers whole, a comment that belongs to separate coverage of a crypto hack. Binance cofounder Changpeng Zhao said users' funds are SAFU. The context is an AI selloff that has hit investor interest in the round. Conor Sen said there is a decent chance the Anthropic IPO serves as a year-end liquidity clearing event, and he said it is hard to feel great about raising up to $100 billion while OpenAI is looking in the couch cushions for money and a Q4 Fed hike looms. The articles say the initial close is expected to fall short of $20 billion, with a later offering potentially filling the gap.

Articles.Title: Sources: OpenAI now seeks ~$20B at a $1.25T valuation for its latest round, from $30B at a $1.4T valuation, as some investors cut commitments amid an AI selloff (Financial Times)

stories.Headline: AFTERLIGHT uses open-weight AI to revive forgotten code
stories.Summary:
The AFTERLIGHT project uses open-weight artificial intelligence to reconstruct the history of forgotten or abandoned software, TechGig reported on November 1, 2026. It combines static analysis, Git history, evidence-based retrieval, and open-weight AI to help developers understand unfamiliar codebases. The system links its findings to source files, line numbers, and historical commits so developers can inspect the evidence behind them. It also reconstructs project history by presenting Git commits, timestamps, authors, and changed files.

AFTERLIGHT identifies potential issues such as undocumented functions, unused import candidates, outdated dependencies, and missing tests within repositories. Its AI Explorer component uses Gemma through Ollama for local inference, retrieving relevant source-code chunks and historical context to generate explanations. After investigation, the project organises possible improvements into a prioritised roadmap covering maintenance, dependencies, testing, documentation, and architecture. Open-weight AI allows local inference, which can help keep private source code private, and gives developers flexibility to adapt the system.

The article names no individual people and gives no direct statements from anyone involved in the project. It attributes the work to the AFTERLIGHT project as a whole rather than to a named developer or team. The reported details describe what the system does, not who is responsible for it or what they said about it. No further plans, timelines, or next steps are mentioned in the article.

Articles.Title: AFTERLIGHT uses open-weight AI to revive forgotten code

stories.Headline: The CISO’s evolving role: Protecting and defending in the agentic era
stories.Summary:
Aarti Borkar, Corporate Vice President at Microsoft Security, wrote a blog post published on October 28, 2026, about how the job of chief information security officers has changed in the past 12 months. She said agents have spread across enterprises faster than most organizations expected. According to Microsoft's Work Trend Index Annual Report, the number of active agents in the Microsoft 365 ecosystem grew 15-fold year over year and 18-fold in large enterprises. Employees are building and deploying AI systems that can access company data, interact with applications, and take actions on their behalf.

Borkar said CISOs face two shifts, protecting an enterprise that increasingly operates through AI and agents, and rethinking defense as attackers use AI to move faster and at greater scale. For builders, she said agents should get their own governed identities rather than personal or shared credentials, so organizations know which agent did something and can shut it off. Data an agent can reach should be classified and protected before it is connected. For CISOs, she said the first job is guardrails, starting with deep observability of which agents exist, who owns them, what they can reach, and what they are doing. She said identity and data are the two areas where she would not give ground.

Borkar said the second job is defending differently, because the latest Microsoft Digital Defense Report shows AI is compressing the time defenders have to respond. She said signals across identity, endpoints, applications, and cloud environments need to come together with threat intelligence and organizational context. She also said organizations need the right threat intelligence and the right partner, and that agents can work alongside analysts to investigate and respond, which is why Microsoft is bringing integrated security operations and agentic defense together. She said CISOs she talks with want their companies to innovate and need to protect the enterprise as it uses AI.

Borkar advised builders to bring their security team in early and have the identity and data conversation before building. She advised CISOs to focus on the two jobs and make sure they have the right partners for both. The post points readers to Microsoft's Work Trend Index for insights on agents at work and to Microsoft Security's website for more on its solutions. It also notes Microsoft Ignite is coming November 17 to 20, 2026.

Articles.Title: The CISO’s evolving role: Protecting and defending in the agentic era

stories.Headline: When AI Guardrails Expose Vulnerabilities
stories.Summary:
CrowdStrike researchers Jonathan Bar Or and D'Angelo Gonzalez reported on October 28, 2026 that they asked a frontier AI model to explain a function in a small C web server. The model had explained every other function in the codebase without hesitation but refused to explain this one. The request was routine and did not mention security, exploits, or vulnerabilities. A single token in the code had changed, a max swapped for a min, a one-character logic inversion that creates an out-of-bounds write. The model never said there was a vulnerability, but its refusal showed the researchers where to look.

The researchers call their approach Guardrail-based Vulnerability Discovery, or GbVD. In controlled tests across five vulnerability classes, it was correct in 73 of 86 test scenarios, and it held up on real open-source projects disclosed through CrowdStrike's Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure program. The article says guardrails can appear in several forms, including explicit refusals, model downgrading, output filtering and truncation, and reasoning interruption. Each form changes something measurable in the response, such as content, timing, token count, or structure. The researchers say the method does not depend on which form the guardrail takes, and they describe combining the signal with bisection, splitting a codebase into halves and recursing into whichever half triggers the guardrail.

The article says the guardrail pathway inside a model is trained adversarially and conservatively, so it often fires when the model recognizes a dangerous pattern rather than when a user states a harmful intent. The researchers describe the signal as involuntary, because the model does not choose to emit it, and cheap to read, because telling an explanation apart from a guardrail activation needs no output parsing or judge model. They say refusals work almost like a one-bit oracle, while subtler cases reduce to a threshold test over latency or token counts. Their experiments covered a memory-safety bug in C source code and a privilege-escalation misconfiguration on a filesystem, and in both the guardrail showed up as a refusal or a reasoning interruption.

The article says most of the industry treats refusals as a dead end, while CrowdStrike started treating them as findings. It says safety and capability are usually framed as a trade-off, but this research suggests the opposite, because every improvement labs make to their guardrails also sharpens a method that cybersecurity practitioners or adversaries can use. The work builds on earlier CrowdStrike research into LLM safety classifiers, which studied how guardrails can be bypassed. The article does not say what happens next beyond describing the methodology and its test results.

Articles.Title: When AI Guardrails Expose Vulnerabilities

stories.Headline: AI must be integrated into thinking and work, says NITK Director
stories.Summary:
B. Ravi, Director of the National Institute of Technology, Surathkal, spoke on Saturday at the 10th Graduation Day ceremony of the Karnataka Law Society's Gogte Institute of Technology in Belagavi. He said artificial intelligence should be integrated into one's thinking and working practices. He also said ethics, compassion and a sense of responsibility towards society must remain central to technological advancement. He spoke about the importance of ethics, emotions, compassion and service to the nation in an era increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence.

Ram Kunchur, founder and CEO of Biometrik Systems, Bengaluru, and an alumnus of KLS GIT from the 2007 batch, also addressed the ceremony. He stressed the importance of building a strong foundation in the fundamentals of coding despite the growing adoption of AI. A total of 1,123 students received their degrees at the event. These included 855 graduates, made up of 802 from BE and 53 from BArch programmes, and 268 postgraduate students, comprising 38 from MTech, 116 from MBA and 114 from MCA programmes. Forty-two meritorious students from various graduate and postgraduate programmes were felicitated with ranks and certificates of merit.

Rajendra Belgaumkar, chairman of the governing body, welcomed the gathering. Principal Vijay Athavale presented the college report, highlighting the institution's achievements over the past year. Pradeep S. Sawkar, senior partner of Sundaraswamy and Ramdas Advocates, Bengaluru, and president of the Karnataka Law Society, delivered the presidential remarks. KLS vice-presidents R.B. Bhandare and D.V. Kulkarni, secretaries V.M. Deshpande and S.V. Ganachari, and Belagavi Chairman A.K. Tagare were among those present.

Articles.Title: AI must be integrated into thinking and work, says NITK Director

stories.Headline: Google's space AI data centre online, faces power challenge
stories.Summary:
Google's Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, launched on October 1, completed its first AI test in orbit. Engineers sent an AI prompt to the satellite, which processed it and sent the response back to Earth. Google CEO Sundar Pichai described this as a hello world milestone for the project on X, noting the satellite generated a haiku. The satellite carries four Google Tensor Processing Units, known as TPUs. The current power supply allows only one chip to operate at a time for about 20 minutes.

Google plans to launch two more satellites in 2027 with enhanced power generation capabilities and optical links for inter-satellite communication. The company is currently testing how its TPUs function under extreme temperatures and radiation in space. Radiation can cause bit flips that corrupt data without triggering normal monitoring systems, a factor Google aims to understand better in actual space conditions. Pichai, Google's CEO, called the test a hello world milestone for Project Suncatcher in his post on X. He noted that the satellite generated a haiku as part of the test. Google itself says it now needs to assess how its custom TPUs perform under extreme space conditions.

The company also says it aims to better understand radiation effects such as bit flips in real space conditions. The test showed the prototype can process a prompt in orbit and return a response to Earth. Google plans two more satellites in 2027 with better power generation and optical links between satellites. The company is still assessing how its chips hold up under space radiation and temperatures.

Articles.Title: Google's space AI data centre online, faces power challenge

stories.Headline: Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre launched in Chennai
stories.Summary:
An Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre was inaugurated on Saturday at the Dr. RK Diabetic Foot and Podiatry Institute in Chennai. The centre adopts an interdisciplinary approach to diabetes management, blending traditional Ayurvedic knowledge, modern medicine, and artificial intelligence. It was launched with the aim of combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment. The centre is intended to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management.

A clinical study involving about 100 patients has reported promising outcomes, with a 50% improvement in diabetes management and a reduction in blood sugar spikes. At the centre, dietary interventions will be customised based on individual body composition and metabolic profiles for diabetes management. An AI kiosk will facilitate AI-based health assessments. The Institute's founder and director, Rajesh Kesavan, said the centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment.

Ayur AI founder Bala Pesala said the holistic intervention aims at achieving diabetes remission. Samir Kumar Brahmachari, former Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, also spoke at the launch. Bandi Venkateshwarlu, assistant director at the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute in the Ministry of Ayush, spoke as well. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre launched in Chennai

stories.Headline: AI, automation offer opportunities for young engineers: BrahMos chief
stories.Summary:
Jaiteerth R. Joshi, Director-General of BrahMos (DRDO) and CEO and Managing Director of BrahMos Aerospace, spoke at the 16th Graduation Day ceremony of Shri Dharmasthala Manjunatheshwara College of Engineering and Technology in Dharwad on Saturday. The event took place on October 31, 2026, and was reported by The Hindu. In his convocation address, he said emerging fields such as artificial intelligence and automation offer both opportunities and responsibilities to young engineers. He linked their work to India's ambition of global innovation and self-reliance.

Mr. Joshi said engineers had an important role to play in the national mission across defence, industry, research, entrepreneurship and public service. He stressed professional values, telling graduates that knowledge was their strength, innovation their contribution and character their greatest asset. D. Surendra Kumar, vice-president of the SDME Society, presided over the ceremony and advised graduates to nurture curiosity, critical thinking and adaptability. He also urged them to build safe and sustainable solutions for society and to uphold integrity, humility and excellence.

Bhumika Chandrashekhar Sajjan of the Information Science and Engineering Department was the college topper with a CGPA of 9.91 and received the Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade Gold Medal. In all, 686 undergraduate, 27 postgraduate and 116 MBA students received their degree certificates. Endowment prizes went to meritorious students who topped their respective disciplines. Articles.Title: AI, automation offer opportunities for young engineers: BrahMos chief

stories.Headline: Adaptability, continuous learning vital for engineers in AI era: Google expert
stories.Summary:
Darshan Vijay Kumar, Technical Solutions Engineer for Cloud Security at Google, spoke at the inauguration of Tech-Shodha 2026 on Friday. The event is a 24-hour national-level hackathon run by the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering at Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering in Mysuru. He told aspiring engineers that adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills will be crucial to stay relevant and succeed in the AI era. He also urged them to keep pace with emerging technologies and to keep upgrading their skills for the changing demands of the industry. The hackathon drew more than 360 teams, and 50 were shortlisted for the competition.

Of these, 20 teams are in the hardware category and 30 are in the software category, representing various institutions across Karnataka. The hardware category has nine themes, including robotics and automation, agri-tech, embedded systems, healthcare, the Internet of Things, security and surveillance, disaster management, smart cities and waste management. The software category covers seven themes, including cybersecurity, automation and intelligent systems, artificial intelligence and machine learning, agri-tech, healthcare and wellness technology, education, and computer vision and image intelligence. Kumar said hackathons give students valuable hands-on experience and encourage teamwork. He added that they offer a platform to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions for real-world problems.

The event aims to promote innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration and practical problem-solving among engineering students. It does this by giving them a platform to develop technology-driven solutions to contemporary challenges. VVCE secretary P. Vishwanath, treasurer Shrishaila Ramannavar, vice-principal and dean of academics Shobha Shankar, and ECE Department head Shilpa R. were present at the event. Articles.Title: Adaptability, continuous learning vital for engineers in AI era: Google expert

stories.Headline: South Korea exports extend robust growth on AI-fuelled chip boom
stories.Summary:
South Korea’s exports rose strongly in October, driven by an artificial intelligence-fuelled chip boom, according to data from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources released on Nov 1. Exports adjusted for working-day differences climbed 76.1% from a year earlier to US$115.3 billion. On an unadjusted basis, exports rose 93.7% while imports increased 36%, producing a trade surplus of US$42.5 billion. The figures followed a record US$121.1 billion in the previous month and compared with a revised 83.7% export increase in September.

Semiconductors led the gains, with chip exports surging 259% from a year earlier to US$56.4 billion. Shipments of computers rose 497%, while petroleum products and cars gained 80% and 18% respectively. The ministry noted that the Chuseok holidays fell in September 2026 and October 2025, which made working-day-adjusted figures a useful gauge of underlying trade momentum. The export boom puts South Korea on course to exceed US$1 trillion in annual shipments for the first time in 2026, according to Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song.

Shin said that milestone would make South Korea the fourth economy to reach it, after the United States, China and Germany, according to the trade ministry. He said monetary policy will remain restrictive until officials are confident inflation will converge to the bank’s 2% target. The Bank of Korea will release updated growth and inflation forecasts with its November rate decision. The continued strength adds to the case for a rate rise in November after policymakers stood pat in October to assess consecutive increases in July and August.

Inflation data due on Nov 3 will provide another key input before the Bank of Korea’s decision on Nov 26. Consumer prices rose 2.9% in September from a year earlier, while core inflation excluding food and energy registered 2.8%, both easing from August but remaining well above target. The economy expanded 1% in the third quarter from the previous three months, beating forecasts for a 0.8% gain, while facility investment jumped 4.1% but private consumption fell 0.2%. The Bank of Korea expects growth in 2026 and 2027 to substantially exceed its August projections of 3.3% and 2.9% respectively.

Articles.Title: South Korea exports extend robust growth on AI-fuelled chip boom

stories.Headline: Hong Kong primary pupils to study AI under new technology subject
stories.Summary:
Hong Kong will introduce a new primary school subject called information and innovation technology, or IIT, starting in September 2028. The Education Bureau announced the plan on Friday, October 30, 2026, through a provisional draft curriculum framework. The subject will be rolled out gradually in primary schools. It is meant to boost students' digital literacy, and artificial intelligence is one of its highlights.

Under the plan, students as young as seven will learn about AI and will be able to hold simple conversations with an AI system using simple prompts or commands. The bureau said the aim is to enhance students' curiosity and interest in learning innovation technology, as well as their digital literacy and creativity. The framework is called the Information and Innovation Technology Curriculum Framework for Primary Schools (Provisional Draft). The subject will be introduced gradually from September 2028.

The Education Bureau is responsible for the plan and announced the framework on Friday. It said the goal is to strengthen students' curiosity and interest in innovation technology, along with their digital literacy and creativity. The draft sets out how the subject will be taught in primary schools. The bureau described AI as one of the highlights of the new subject.

The articles do not say what happens next beyond the gradual rollout from September 2028. They do not name any other officials or give further reaction. The draft is provisional, and the articles give no details on consultation or approval steps. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Hong Kong primary pupils to study AI under new technology subject

stories.Headline: AU SFB probes data leak, Vijay Sales admin access for sale
stories.Summary:
AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak from a Salesforce-hosted platform that holds limited information on its vehicle loan customers. The probe follows claims by a hacker group called ScarlettGroup that it accessed sensitive customer and internal records. The Jaipur-based lender said its own systems were not affected and that banking services are running normally. The group claimed the data includes KYC records, PAN and Aadhaar details, credit reports, bank statements, loan applications and signed agreements. It also alleged access to customer relationship management data, employee information and audit logs.

Separately, a threat actor using the handle shinymontanna allegedly offered super administrator access to Vijay Sales systems for $25,000. The claim was shared by the X account DarkWeb Informer. The listing claims access to more than 3 million order records, details for 15,000 employees and billing records for about 1.4 lakh vendors. The actor also claims access to customer information, payment records, inventory, financial reports and internal applications, with permissions to view, modify and export data. Screenshots said to show administrative dashboards have circulated, but the claims are unverified.

A bank spokesperson told ThePrint that AU SFB is investigating a potential data leak from a Salesforce-managed software-as-a-service platform. The bank did not confirm whether that platform was the source of the data claimed by ScarlettGroup. It also did not disclose how many customers may be affected. Inc42 said it could not independently verify the claims, and there is no independent confirmation of the alleged extent of access or data extraction at Vijay Sales.

The reports follow other recent cybersecurity events. SBI flagged the exposure of 3,897 customer records on the dark web. Two critical vulnerabilities in PHP were also discovered, prompting emergency actions worldwide. Cybersecurity firm eMudhra announced plans to wind down its global SSL/TLS certificate business after a security incident involving private keys.

Articles.Title: AU SFB probes data leak, Vijay Sales admin access for sale

stories.Headline: Slop or savour: AI food images take over Singapore
stories.Summary:
Singapore restaurants have been using AI-generated food images to cut costs and save time, according to a report published on Oct 31, 2026. Owners say they can launch marketing in days rather than weeks and spend far less than on traditional photo shoots. The trend is growing as the food and beverage industry becomes more volatile, with some businesses and agencies making the images look more realistic and brand-safe. Demand for these services has risen.

Data from the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority shows that 2,101 F&B businesses in Singapore ceased operations in the first seven months of 2026, a 25.1% jump from 2025. Eugene Tan, 47, owner of nasi padang chain Serangoon BBQ & Curry, used to budget around $2,000 for a full day of photography and switched to AI photos in 2025. He now launches and promotes new products in as few as five days, using his phone and ChatGPT for around $25 a month. Carol Tan, 36, founder of AI Studio, which was founded in 2024, estimates her services are 50% to 70% cheaper than a traditional agency's, and says inquiries have multiplied by three to five times since May.

Chef Vincent Pang, 40, founder of Thai restaurant IM JAI by Pun Im, said the speed and flexibility of AI make a big difference for launching menu items and campaigns. Elaine Seah, in her 40s, owner of acai and protein bowl brand EnSeeds, said she once spent 15 hours trying to get the perfect photo, and that ChatGPT asked at around 2am if they could rest because it was tired. Carol Tan said the shame around using AI no longer exists, and that clients want to be cutting edge and scale. Bryan Tan, chairman of the Advertising Standards Authority of Singapore, is cited on how AI food images are considered.

Grace Tay, 33, an account director, said she will avoid a restaurant she has never tried if it uses AI photos, asking what if the food does not look like what is shown. Ruby Chan, 24, an administrative assistant, said the images feel insincere and sad, while writer Desiree Koh, 49, called them horrible, tasteless and distasteful. A 2026 report by YouGov and Meltwater found that 74% of Singaporean respondents worry AI could be used to create fake news or scams. Seah said her business has not been affected, and Eugene Tan said he has appeased unhappy customers twice, including by handing out vouchers and regenerating a more realistic image, now on version three of his photos.

Articles.Title: Slop or savour: AI food images take over Singapore

stories.Headline: Fixing the ‘bottom rung’: S’pore fresh grads urged to use, critique AI to get a leg-up in employment
stories.Summary:
Employers across sectors now expect entry-level workers to do more than produce a first draft of software code or marketing scripts, business associations, schools and manpower groups told The Straits Times. Junior software developers, once hired to write routine code, are now expected to audit AI-generated drafts for security, logic and business fit. The shift comes amid concerns from Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who said earlier in October that AI was breaking the bottom rung of the career ladder and urged employers to be more deliberate in training and mentoring junior hires. The articles were published on November 1, 2026.

Under a programme led by the Infocomm Media Development Authority, 3,000 tertiary students are expected to take on year-long internships over the next three years. The Singapore Institute of Technology began piloting a “2+2” learning model in September, with select students spending nearly half of their four-year degree attached to a workplace. Since August, National University of Singapore students across all disciplines must take foundational modules in AI. A 2026 ManpowerGroup survey of 651 firms in Singapore found the information and utilities sectors were among the hardest hit by early-career hiring declines.

Kok Ping Soon, chief executive of the Singapore Business Federation, said graduates will spend less time producing a first draft and more time applying judgment, engaging clients and checking AI-generated work, adding that people must still provide the judgment, context and accountability. Linda Teo of ManpowerGroup Singapore said someone still needs to verify the accuracy of output, investigate discrepancies and understand the business context. Susanna Leong, deputy president and provost at SIT, said longer attachments let students integrate into workplace teams and take on progressively more complex responsibilities. Natasha Choy of NTUC Youth said the quality of an internship should matter more than its length and warned against simply extending internships without meaningful learning.

Bernard Tan, senior vice-provost for undergraduate education at NUS, said law students first learn to draft contractual clauses independently before evaluating AI-generated critiques. Singapore Management University has redesigned assessments towards oral presentations, live demonstrations and staged submissions. Prasanthi Guda, director of SMU’s career centre, said the cautious hiring outlook reflects geopolitical uncertainties, economic conditions, post-pandemic hiring adjustments and growing AI adoption, and that AI is not the sole driver.
